_meta.indication: Treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma who have received at least four prior lines of therapy, including a proteasome inhibitor, an immunomodulatory agent, and an anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 1/2 single-arm, open-label, multicenter, multicohort trial of linvoseltamab monotherapy
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with RRMM who received 4 or more prior lines of therapy including a PI, an IMiD, and an anti-CD38 mAb (efficacy population)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall response rate (ORR), an intermediate clinical endpoint, supported by duration of response (DOR)
pivotal_trials.result: ORR 70.0% (95% CI: 58.7%, 79.7%); CR or better 45%. At the original data cutoff (median follow-up 11.3 months) the median DOR was not reached; with updated data at the resubmission (median follow-up 21.7 months) the median DOR was 21.0 months (95% CI: 19.0, NE).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=20%) were musculoskeletal pain, CRS, cough, upper respiratory tract infection, diarrhea, fatigue, pneumonia, nausea, headache, and dyspnea. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 74% and fatal adverse reactions in 7% of patients. CRS occurred in 46% and neurologic toxicity in 54%.
target_moa: Bispecific BCMA-directed and CD3-directed T-cell engager that forms a synapse between T-cells and BCMA-expressing myeloma cells, resulting in T-cell activation and killing of myeloma cells
modality: Bispecific antibody (BCMA x CD3 T-cell engager)

boxed_warning.content: Cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and neurologic toxicity, including immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS), which can be serious or life-threatening

rems.type: LYNOZYFIC is available only through a restricted program under a REMS called the LYNOZYFIC REMS because of the risks of CRS and neurologic toxicity, including ICANS

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not presented at an advisory committee meeting and no external consultations were utilized in the review.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Response rate (ORR), an intermediate clinical endpoint, and durability of response

citations.quote: This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on response rate and durability of response [see *Clinical Studies* (14)]. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in confirmatory trial(s).

summary.text: Linvoseltamab received Orphan Drug Designation and Fast Track Designation and the BLA received Priority review; it was granted accelerated approval based on ORR and durability of response from the single-arm Study 1826, with the randomized Phase 3 LINKER-MM3 (Study 2245) as the required confirmatory trial. A Complete Response was issued in August 2024 for manufacturing issues before approval on resubmission.

This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on response rate and durability of response [see *Clinical Studies* (14)]. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in confirmatory trial(s).
However, the FDA identified significant manufacturing issues precluding approval and a Complete Response was issued on August 20, 2024. The Applicant resubmitted the BLA on January 10, 2025.

requirement.text: 4848-1 Complete a randomized clinical trial in patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma. Patients should be randomized to receive livoseltamab compared to standard therapy for relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma. The primary endpoint should be progression-free survival and key secondary endpoints should include overall response rate and overall survival. The trial should enroll a sufficiently representative study population to allow for generalizability of the result to the U.S. patient population with multiple myeloma.
